note: TRIGGER REPLACED 2026-10-16, after review found the recorded one could not reach the defect. The old trigger was offsets() over a flat OR of two phrases, and the reason it was harmless is structural, not accidental: fts3EvalRestart walks the subtree of pNear, the phrase's most senior NEAR ancestor, so with no NEAR operator every phrase has pNear = itself and a restart can only free the poslist of the phrase being fetched -- whose address is stored after that fetch returns. Probe site 45 measured the old order as SAVE x2, 6 reads, SAVE, RESTART, SAVE, 4 reads: one restart, and every group of reads preceded by its own save. (The 2026-10-11 note said three restarts, all after both calls; that was wrong in its reason as well as its count.) Three facts pin down a trigger that does reach it: the freed and the saved phrase must share a NEAR group; the restart branch is reached only below an OR and only for an incremental phrase that is off-row; and fts3EvalTestExpr zeroes a non-matching NEAR group's poslists before any auxiliary function runs, unless an AND operand to its left fails first, because bHit = (TestExpr(pLeft) && TestExpr(pRight) && NearTest()) short-circuits. Hence (xx AND ("pp1 pp2" NEAR/3 qq)) OR rr. Evidence, all 2026-10-16: host ASan as in live_proof; probe site 45, which prints the pointer at the save, the free and the read, shows on native memsys5 SAVE p=base+1, RESTART frees p=base bFreeList=1, then two reads at base+1 and base+2, the same block ASan names; witnesses=0 because memsys5 reissues the block to the reload that follows the free, the same address-oracle blind spot as case 07. On stock memsys5 the stale read completes and the garbage makes offsets() return SQLITE_CORRUPT -- rows=1, last_step_rc=11, "database disk image is malformed" on an in-memory database built three statements earlier. A negative control settles the direction: with the NEAR operands swapped, so the restart happens before the save, host ASan is silent.
